The structure of NiCoGeO₄ crystallizes in the monoclinic space group C2/c (No. 15), with a unit cell containing 40 atoms—Ni₈Co₈Ge₈O₃₂—distributed over six independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis identifies Co and Ge centers as octahedral, each coordinated by six O neighbors, while Ni centers show a four-coordinate O environment. Validated polyhedron-sharing relations reveal edge-sharing between Co and Ge octahedra, and corner-sharing between Co and Ni polyhedra. The geometric neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component spanning all 40 sites.
